classification.difficultyReason: Organise the taught feature-finding procedure without separate prompts, interpret leading signs in differently written factors and repeated roots, and translate intercepts and vertices into sketches.

content.prompt: Sketch these parabolas. Clearly label the vertex and intercepts.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the parabola is concave up.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(-5)(-1)\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$, use the null factor law:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-5)(x-1)\\x&=5\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
For the vertex:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{1+5}{2}\\x&=3\\y&=(3-5)(3-1)\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening curve through $(1,0)$, $(5,0)$ and $(0,5)$, with vertex $(3,-4)$.

answer.worked:
The coefficient of $x^2$ is $2>0$, so the parabola is concave up.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(5)(1)\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$, use the null factor law:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(2x+5)(x+1)\\x&=-\frac52\text{ or }-1\end{align*}$$
For the vertex:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-\frac52+(-1)}{2}\\x&=-\frac74\\y&=\left(2\left(-\frac74\right)+5\right)\left(-\frac74+1\right)\\y&=\frac32\left(-\frac34\right)\\y&=-\frac98\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening curve through $(-\frac52,0)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,5)$, with vertex $(-\frac74,-\frac98)$.

The coefficient of $x^2$ is $2\times\frac12=1>0$, so the parabola is concave up.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(5)(1)\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$, use the null factor law:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(2x+5)\left(\frac12x+1\right)\\x&=-\frac52\text{ or }-2\end{align*}$$
For the vertex:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-\frac52+(-2)}{2}\\x&=-\frac94\\y&=\left(2\left(-\frac94\right)+5\right)\left(\frac12\left(-\frac94\right)+1\right)\\y&=\frac12\left(-\frac18\right)\\y&=-\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening curve through $(-\frac52,0)$, $(-2,0)$ and $(0,5)$. Its vertex $(-\frac94,-\frac1{16})$ lies just below the $x$-axis.
